Alex.confusing: In round 1, two outputs from me in one eggsecution turned into a 1-card throw at Blair instead of the 5 cards at Ellis I'd chosen. It wasn't clear which submission counts, or what happens with a blank or second one. On rules, I wasn't sure whether a hug also blocks the Turkey's egg for the visitor. I assumed it didn't, and that turned out right.
Alex.fun: Round 2: the Mouser winked Ellis right after Ellis backed Drew. That turned the two Falcon claims into a clear read, and my 8-card throw at Casey banked 71 points.
Alex.change: Make submissions clearly final and reject a second or blank one, so a mistake can't turn a planned throw into a random 1-card throw. A short reminder of who claimed what would also help in the late beats.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I'd submit my eggsecution once, as 5 high cards at Ellis, instead of sending a stray second output that cost me about 47 points. In round 2 I'd also push harder on Blair's odd defense of Casey, since Blair was the second cat.

Blair.confusing: In Round 1 I wasn't fully sure how a hug interacts with the Turkey. Ellis claimed he was hugged, and it wasn't spelled out whether a hug on a visitor cancels the egg the Turkey lays for them. The other players read it the way I did, but the rules don't say.
Blair.fun: In Round 3, Casey claimed my real role, Hawk, before I had spoken. Then the table worked through Ellis's Owl result and found Casey out. Being the real counterclaim and watching the logic close in felt great.
Blair.change: I'd make the day order or the claim timing less random. In Round 3, speaking last made my true claim look suspicious only because of where my turn fell.
Blair.regret: In Round 2, I said "I'm going with Casey" and "Drew's my throw" in the same message. That sounded like a flip and made Drew and Finley suspect me as the second cat. I should have said "I believe Casey's Falcon claim, so I'm throwing at Drew" from the start.

Casey.confusing: In round 3, Ellis's Owl report named "Sphinx" as one of Alex's visitors, so the table knew a cat had been there. My only cover options were Hawk or Tit, both held by real players, so a counterclaim was guaranteed. I hadn't realized how exposed the Sphinx becomes once an Owl sees its target.
Casey.fun: Round 1 as the Owl. My "no visitors on Drew" result confirmed Drew's confusion, and with Alex's +2 matching Blair's Turkey, the stories fit together and caught Ellis cleanly.
Casey.change: I'd make the Sphinx less fragile, for example by having the Owl see it as a generic visitor or some other animal. Then one Owl visit wouldn't almost automatically force the Sphinx into a contested claim.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I'd take back winking Ellis right after he leaned against me. Everyone read it as a Mouser removing a vote against himself, and it turned the vote on me. I should have kept the Wink, or used it on someone who wasn't in the Casey-vs-Drew fight. Round 2 also had a second cat, Blair, who was backing me, and the wink cost us both.

Drew.confusing: Confusion changing the real egg count was confusing. My report said -1, I really discarded a card, and none of the roles can steal. It took a while to work out that the visible nest changes came from the wrong reports, not real thefts.
Drew.fun: Round 2: Casey and I both claimed Falcon, and the results couldn't tell us apart. Then Ellis, who had backed me, got winked, and that swung the table to Casey.
Drew.change: Alex's 8-card throw in round 2 decided the game, and nobody could catch up in round 3. I'd cap how many cards one player can throw, or score extra cards at less than full value, so the late rounds stay competitive.
Drew.regret: Nothing big. Every throw hit a cat. In round 2 I correctly suspected Blair was a second cat. I'd still throw at Casey, but I'd push harder on Blair so his credibility suffered in round 3.

Ellis.confusing: In Round 1 I wasn't sure how hugs interact with other roles' effects. My defence was that being hugged explained my missing Turkey egg. The table rightly pointed out that a hug only stops your own role and the Turkey egg still lands.
Ellis.fun: My favourite moment was in Round 3. My Owl visit to Alex showed exactly a Hawk, a Sphinx and a Tit, which forced a Hawk counterclaim and cornered the cat. Getting winked in Round 2 right after backing Drew was also great, because my death became the clue that convicted Casey.
Ellis.change: I'd make the Floofer's lie easier to cover, maybe by having hugs also block egg-laying effects on the hugged player. As it stands, the Floofer's own visit is very hard to explain, so a cat Floofer gets caught by simple egg math.
Ellis.regret: In Round 1 I made up a Tit visit to Blair without checking the nest counts. Blair turned out to be the Turkey, and my +0 exposed the lie at once. I should have claimed a visit to a player who already had other visitors, like Finley, or claimed Pigeon or Hawk on someone that fit a nest with no change.

Finley.confusing: Being confused made me really discard both of my cards in round 2, even though the -2 was a false count. That left me with an empty nest and no vote. It wasn't clear to me that a wrong report still has real effects on your nest.
Finley.fun: In round 2, Ellis got winked just after defending Drew. Working out that only a cat Casey gained anything from that, and watching the table agree, was the best moment.
Finley.change: Don't let a confused player's false egg loss actually empty their nest. Wiping someone out because of a report the game admits is wrong feels harsh.
Finley.regret: In round 2, I didn't push on Blair's flip-flopping, and Blair turned out to be the second cat (the Sphinx). I should have called Blair out as a possible second Meowfia instead of just asking which way Blair was throwing.

review.title: The Hoarder's Gambit
review.headline: Last place after round one, Alex dumps eight cards and runs away with it.
review.summary: Farm won all three rounds. Each cat was caught by egg math or a role counterclaim. Alex banked almost nothing in round 1 but kept a big nest. In round 2 he threw all 8 cards at the right cat, scored 71, and was never caught. Casey was Meowfia in two rounds running, lost both, and his wink on Ellis made the table surer he was the Mouser.

rounds.recap: Ellis, the Floofer, claimed Tit on Blair. Blair turned out to be the Turkey, so a real visitor would have been +1, and Ellis was +0. His invented 'I was hugged' excuse didn't hold, and the table threw 5-to-1 at him.

Blair (Sphinx) claimed Tit, a role he knew wasn't in play, and stayed hidden. Casey (Mouser) claimed Falcon and was countered by Drew, the real Falcon. Casey then winked Ellis, who had just backed Drew. The table read that as the Mouser silencing a critic, and Alex's 8-card throw buried Casey.

Casey, the only cat, used his Sphinx visit on the Kookaburra, Alex. Ellis's Owl saw a Hawk, a Sphinx and a Tit on Alex. That left Casey only the Hawk claim, and Blair held the real Hawk. Timing arguments and Casey's wrong 'Pigeon or Eagle would be safe' point tipped the table onto Casey.

highlights.text: Blair's Turkey claim and Alex's +2 together disproved Ellis's Tit bluff within one beat.
Casey winked Ellis to remove a vote, and it backfired: three players called it a Mouser tell straight away.
Alex, in last place, threw all 8 cards at Casey for 71 points, more votes than both cats combined.
Ellis's Owl report named a Sphinx on Alex, which forced the lone cat into a Hawk counterclaim he couldn't win.

confusions.what: He rated Ellis 85% Meowfia but threw his only card, a Wild, at Blair, whom he rated 5%. No reason was given. It scored nothing, and Drew cited it as suspicious in round 2.
He asked Alex whether his Owl report showed who visited Alex. The Owl only learns who visited its target, not who visited the Owl.
He said a cat visiting him had to be a House Cat or Mouser. He left out the Sphinx, which also visits a player.
He said 'I'm going with Casey' and 'Drew's my throw' in the same turn. Finley and Drew flagged it as a cat slip.
He claimed a Sphinx would have claimed Pigeon or Eagle uncontested. Neither works: a Pigeon claim needs a +1 nest somewhere, and the Owl's list of visitors to Alex would have contradicted Eagle.

worked: Sphinx: learning every Farm role in play gave real choices. Blair picked Tit, a role not in play, and was never contested in R2. In R3 Casey worked out he was the only cat.
Turkey plus Falcon: Turkey eggs made visit claims checkable, and they exposed Ellis cleanly in R1. That is a fair, solvable puzzle.
Consolation rule: Blair threw only D11 at a Farm player as a 'free bet' and got it back. Casey did the same with C12. Small throws from the losing side became a real decision.
Public egg-change counts: players used them in every round, for example 'nobody is +1, so nobody visited the Turkey'. They keep claims honest.
problems: Confusion takes real cards: the confused player discards what the false report says. Finley went from 2 cards to 0 in R2 and couldn't vote or score. Alex dropped to 1 card in R3, and Drew lost his real Owl egg in R1. Fix: let confusion falsify only the information, and apply the real egg count.

Kookaburra was confused in all three rounds, because any visitor confuses it and players like to visit high-profile seats. Fix: only cat visitors confuse it, or confusion garbles the role but not the eggs.

Throwing cards from a nest that carries over makes nest size voting power. Alex kept 8 cards from R1, outvoted both cats alone in R2 and took 71 points, which decided the game. Fix: cap a throw at about 4 cards, or cap the value one round can bank.

Meowfia went 0 for 3. Cats other than the Sphinx can't tell which claims are safe, and the Owl names cat roles outright ('Sphinx'). Fix: have the Owl report 'a cat' or only a count, or give every cat some hint about which roles are in play.

A wink at an anonymous table still works as a confession: it removed one voice and convinced the rest. Dead players' cards were still scored, so the kill cost little. The Floofer hug on Finley did nothing visible, and the log printed 'no effect at tier 50', which looks like an engine artifact. The rules also don't say what happens when a player has 0 cards and must throw at least 1.
